Consistent with prior studies, we focused on behavioral and fMRI responses to items in the International Affective Picture System (IAPS), a well-characterized stimulus set often used in the study of affect processing that captures the richness of multi-dimensional information encoded by affective stimuli.

We used multi-voxel pattern classification (MVPC) to identify whole-brain patterns of functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI)-derived neural activations that reliably predicted dimensional properties of affect (valence and arousal) for visual stimuli viewed by a normative sample (  n   = 32) of demographically diverse, healthy adults.
